records.heading: Ground rehearsal, not launch
records.claim: The Apollo 1 crew was conducting the plugs-out countdown rehearsal with the command module sealed on the launch pad.
records.boundary: The unfueled launch vehicle did not make the cabin or its escape provisions safe.
records.evidence_role: Primary investigation — NASA-hosted copy of the 1967 Board report
records.context_role: NASA 2022 retrospective — contextual, not contemporary evidence
records.catalog_note: Historical crew photographs illustrate the people, not the test's engineering conditions. No photographs are reproduced here.

records.heading: The oxygen environment
records.claim: The Board reported a 100-percent oxygen atmosphere at 16.7 psia during the test, with combustible materials inside the command module.
records.boundary: Oxygen supported rapid combustion; the atmosphere itself does not identify an ignition spark, and the ground-test pressure was not orbital flight pressure.
records.catalog_note: A spacecraft image catalog entry is not instrumentation establishing cabin pressure.

records.heading: Recorded fire sequence
records.claim: The Review Board documented the brief sequence of fire reports, pressure rise and command-module rupture.
records.boundary: The Board's observed time markers are not continuous measurements or evidence of the exact ignition point.
records.evidence_role: Primary investigation — Fire Chronology and Data Analysis
records.catalog_note: NASA photo S66-58038 depicts the crew in 1966; it is NOT an instrument chronology, time-series dataset or proof of these times.

records.heading: The inward-opening hatch
records.claim: The Board described the inward-opening hatch and why the fire-driven rise in pressure prevented prompt emergency egress.
records.boundary: The hatch compounded multiple hazards; it was not the sole cause of the fire.
records.evidence_role: Primary investigation — Escape and hatch findings
records.context_role: NASA 2017 exhibit account — later explanation of hatch redesign
records.catalog_note: A 2017 exhibit photo may document a displayed hatch; it does not independently prove the 1967 failure mechanism.

records.heading: Probable electrical arc, no identified spark
records.claim: The Board regarded an electrical arc as the most probable initiator, but did not conclusively identify the specific source.
records.boundary: Do not promote a candidate wire, arc location or theory to a conclusively established cause.
records.evidence_role: Primary investigation — Cause of the Apollo 204 Fire
records.catalog_note: Post-fire photographs are damage records, not proof of the initiating arc.

records.heading: Later redesign and flammability tests
records.claim: NASA's later historical account reports 102 deliberate ignitions of Command Module Boilerplate 1224 during December 1967–February 1968 tests.
records.boundary: These were later deliberate engineering tests, not 102 ignitions during the January 1967 accident.
records.evidence_role: NASA 2018 retrospective reporting the post-fire flammability program
records.context_role: NASA 2017 exhibit account — redesigned hatch context
records.catalog_note: The 2017 hatch exhibit photograph does not document the 102 test ignitions.
